precedent.effect: With an explicit clause_id the error was local and per-case (20/34 partial). Deriving it from the span turned clause identity into a global inferred property, so one repeated span invalidates the whole graph: 34/34 total.
precedent.lesson: Deriving an identifier does not remove the constraint, it moves it where the schema cannot reach. If the constraint stays fatal it must become structure (S1); if it cannot become structure it must not be fatal (S2).
precedent.summary: Same failure class recurred, and the mitigation raised its severity.
precedent.v2641_live: 20 of 34 cases had clause_ids as their only error, because prompt and schema did not declare the consecutivity the validator required (handover section 2).
precedent.v265_response: V26.5 removed clause_id from the LLM output and derived it from span order (handover section 3).

proven: Both /tmp artifacts match their expected SHA-256 exactly.
All 20 pinned runtime/postbatch dependencies are byte-intact; 14/14 cross-hashes agree.
Transport was flawless: 34/34 HTTP 200, 0 errors, 0 exception chains, phase=complete, 0 retries.

The span-collision code fires iff two anchors (projections + unsupported_clauses) share one (start,end) pair.
Three distinct schema-VALID frames are rejected by the frozen adapter with the two observed codes, proving the invariants are outside the constrained-decoding surface.
The gold fixture expects at most one projection per graph (31 supported/1 projection, 3 typed_ambiguity), so the encoding CAN represent the correct answer for every case.
status was never 'unsupported' in the 33 adapter failures, because that branch raises a different, never-observed code.
Case 7 ('neredeyim') has segment_count=1, so the only possible span is (1,1) and any two anchors collide by arithmetic necessity; the model provably emitted >=2 anchors there.
The dependency check demands exact span tuple equality, not containment: widening the dependency span to equal the projection span is accepted.
The opaque-case-to-query join is cryptographically verified 34/34 on segment_count and segment_layout_sha256.

The same failure class was already recorded in the V26.4.1 live (20/34 cases failing only on clause_ids); V26.5 responded by removing clause_id and deriving it from span order, which converted a partial per-case error into a total structural one.
root_cause: The compact encoding removed clause_id and promoted the source span to surrogate primary key for clause identity. Decoding therefore requires span-injectivity over projections union unsupported_clauses, and exact span equality between a dependency and its projection. Neither invariant is expressible in JSON Schema, so constrained decoding cannot enforce them; both live only in prompt prose; both abort fatally before any semantic validation. One field carries two incompatible semantics at once: clause identity and evidential grounding.
scope: typed-registry Phase-1 K1/34 live post-mortem, offline only

successor.S1: Move clause identity into the document structure: clauses[] each owning exactly one projection and its dependencies[]. Clause identity is the array position, so no numeric label is emitted and compactness is preserved; the span degrades to pure evidence. Makes the 32-case failure schema-unrepresentable and dissolves the dependency-span check by containment.
successor.S2: Invariant rule (the generalizable part): every fatal decoder invariant must be either expressible in the response schema or demoted to non-fatal. An invariant that is neither is a latent zero-yield run.
successor.S3: Non-censoring diagnosis: do not abort at the first stage; run stages best-effort and report every stage's codes.
successor.S4: Persist a bounded structural digest on failure (status, counts of atoms/projections/dependencies/unsupported clauses, span multiset shape). No query material. This is exactly what is missing today.
